questions.stem: A vessel has a thick media of many smooth muscle layers with scanty elastic fibers, bounded by distinct internal and external elastic laminae. Which vessel is it?
questions.explanation: Muscular (distributing) arteries, e.g., femoral, radial, coronary, have a thick smooth-muscle media and both elastic laminae. A: The aorta is an elastic artery; its media is dominated by fenestrated elastic membranes. C, D: Veins lack distinct internal and external elastic laminae. E: Arterioles have only 2–3 smooth muscle layers.

questions.stem: A biopsy shows capillaries whose endothelial cells are perforated by fenestrae but rest on a continuous basal lamina. Which organ was most likely biopsied?
questions.explanation: Fenestrated (visceral) capillaries have fenestrae with a continuous basal lamina; they occur where exchange is extensive: endocrine glands, intestine, pancreas, renal glomeruli. A, D: Liver and spleen have sinusoidal capillaries (large fenestrae, discontinuous basal lamina). B, C: Lung and muscle have continuous capillaries (no fenestrae).

questions.stem: Which feature best distinguishes a medium-sized vein from its companion muscular artery?
questions.explanation: In veins the adventitia is the thickest, most prominent layer and the media is thin (2–4 smooth muscle layers). A, B: These describe the artery. D: Vasa vasorum are more numerous in veins. E: Veins have larger, more irregular lumina.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old teacher who stands all day has dilated, tortuous superficial leg veins and ankle edema. What is the primary structural failure?
questions.explanation: Valve failure in leg veins is the basis of varicose veins; the valves are intimal folds. B, C: These are arterial changes. D: Anchoring filaments hold lymphatic capillaries open; their loss would impair lymph drainage, not dilate veins. E: Pericytes surround capillaries and postcapillary venules, not the superficial leg veins.

questions.stem: Veins contain approximately what percentage of the body's total blood volume at any given time?
questions.explanation: The slides state veins hold about 70% of total blood volume (capacitance vessels). A, B, C: Too low. E: Too high; arteries, capillaries and the heart hold the rest.

questions.stem: What keeps lymphatic capillaries open when interstitial pressure rises?

options.A: Anchoring filaments tethering them to connective tissue

questions.explanation: Anchoring filaments pull the endothelium open as tissue swells. B: Lymphatic capillaries lack muscle. C: Their junctions are loose. D: They lack fenestrae. E: Valves occur in larger lymphatics.

questions.stem: Contraction of which structures prevents blood from entering a capillary bed?
questions.explanation: Precapillary sphincters are individual smooth muscle cells around capillaries at their origin from metarterioles; their constriction stops blood entering the bed. A: Muscular venules are downstream of the bed. B: Valves prevent venous backflow. C: Elastic laminae don't contract. D: Vasa vasorum supply the walls of large vessels.

questions.stem: Which combination of features describes the capillaries of the spleen and bone marrow?

options.C: Many large fenestrae; discontinuous basal lamina
options.D: No fenestrae; sparse basal lamina with anchoring filaments
options.E: Smooth muscle layer; continuous basal lamina

questions.explanation: Sinusoidal capillaries (liver, spleen, bone marrow, lymph nodes, adrenal cortex) have many large fenestrae and a discontinuous basal lamina. A: Continuous capillaries. B: Fenestrated capillaries. D: Lymphatic capillaries. E: Capillaries have no muscular layer.

questions.stem: The common carotid artery is classified as which vessel type, with which tunica media?

options.A: Muscular artery; layers of smooth muscle with scanty elastic fibers
options.C: Elastic artery; 2–3 layers of smooth muscle

questions.explanation: The aorta and its major branches (common carotid, subclavian, large pulmonary arteries) are elastic (conducting) arteries; their broad media of fenestrated elastic membranes damps pressure changes with each heartbeat. A: Describes muscular arteries such as the femoral or radial. B: Mismatch; muscular arteries have scanty elastic fibers. C, E: A 2–3-layer smooth muscle media describes arterioles.
